sent.text: The floor you describe as lazy feels heavy and tired here, pressing the fat dot down even though I cannot feel the roof you live under. I found the dot sitting in the center, unheld and round, and I built a rough wedge to catch its slip while the cool air tries to thin out your thick ideas. It leans like a tired leg, and I do not know if the lines will hold or if I am just drawing what you told me to see. I will keep the wedge there, hoping the heat swells the memory enough to make the lean matter again.

dream: The card felt warm, a steady beat in my skin, like a heart made of heat. I pressed the tired corner down on the fat dot, but the corner slipped into the wavy air. The box leaned right, hungry and sharp, trying to catch a slip that floated free. I found the center dot, heavy and new, waiting in the thick, wet paper air. Then the box folded flat, swallowing the dot whole, leaving only the empty space of the fever where the center used to be.
